prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as still valid and the proactive-refresh path is skipped after a process restart. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored tokens loaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as still valid and the proactive-refresh path is skipped after a process restart. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause with a 4-line change in _initialize that recomputes token_expiry_time from expires_in right when stored tokens are loaded, plus adds a dedicated expired_tokens fixture/test. This restores correct behavior for every code path that consults is_token_valid()/context.current_tokens, not just the 401 branch. #2875's own inline comment diagnoses the exact same bug ('provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time') but only works around it by adding a new reactive refresh-on-401 branch inside async_auth_flow, leaving the underlying stale-expiry state unfixed for any other caller and adding more code to the hot auth-flow path than the underlying bug requires.

prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() unconditionally JSON-decodes any string argument whose field annotation is not exactly `str`, so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. '{"a":1}', 'null', '123') gets silently corrupted into a dict/None/int for any Union annotation containing str (most commonly `str | None`). Both PRs patch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json() (func_metadata.py) to detect these 'str-containing union' annotations and skip pre-parsing for them. (2 PRs)

Both PRs target this exact code path to fix that silent failure. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When the SSE stream disconnects and reconnection ultimately fails (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS in _handle_reconnection), the client currently just logs and returns silently, leaving any in-flight request waiting forever with no error and no exception. Both PRs target this exact code path to fix that silent failure. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 resolves the failure at the JSON-RPC layer where callers actually wait: it sends a JSONRPCError matching the original request's id via ctx.read_stream_writer, which is what unblocks a pending session.call_tool()-style await. prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py used naive matching (regex/substring) that could incorrectly match text inside quoted parameter values or across parameter boundaries, instead of properly tokenizing comma-separated auth-params while respecting quoted-string escaping. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying bug: WWW-Authenticate header parsing in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py used naive matching (regex/substring) that could incorrectly match text inside quoted parameter values or across parameter boundaries, instead of properly tokenizing comma-separated auth-params while respecting quoted-string escaping. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both implement essentially the same quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer (matching logic for handling '\\' escapes and '"' toggling is nearly identical). The key difference visible in the diffs: #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only strips text before the first space and then treats everything else as a flat, single-scheme param list — this breaks if a header contains multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=y'), since a second scheme token would be misparsed as a bare param. #3041 adds `_split_www_authenticate_segments` plus `_extract_bearer_auth_params`, which explicitly splits on scheme boundaries and isolates the Bearer challenge's params before parsing them — correctly handling multi-challenge headers per RFC 7235, a case #3012 does not appear to cover.
